sections.h2: Where is a deed recorded in Perry County, KY?
sections.html:
Every deed, mortgage and release for property in Perry County is filed with the County Clerk in Hazard, at 481 Main Street, Suite 102. The clerk's contact block lists 606-439-0557 and weekday hours of 8:00 AM to 4:00 PM, and the county government's directory gives 606-436-4614 as the clerk's office line. Because older pages on the clerk's site show slightly different opening times, a short call before a trip saves a wasted drive.

Recording does not have to happen at the counter. The clerk's land records page names four e-recording services (Indecomm, CSC, Simplifile and ePN). Lenders, attorneys and title agents can also subscribe to eCCLIX, the clerk's online index, to pull recorded documents without visiting the courthouse.

sections.h2: What does a Kentucky deed need before the Perry County Clerk accepts it?
sections.html:
The clerk checks a deed against a fixed list, and a missing item means the deed is returned. County clerk offices across Kentucky, Pike County's among them, publish the same checklist:

  • Names and mailing addresses of the seller (grantor) and the buyer (grantee).
  • A legal description of the property and the source of title.
  • A preparation statement naming who drafted the deed.
  • A return mail address for the recorded original.
  • An in-care-of address where the property tax bill for the year of transfer can be sent, required on all deeds under KRS 382.135.
  • A consideration statement, sworn and notarized by both parties, with the grantor's signature acknowledged before a notary.

Gifts and nominal-price transfers need a different statement, one that gives the estimated fair cash value. Deeds that only convey utility easements, correct an earlier deed between the same parties, or pass property through a divorce case are excused from the consideration statement. For an inherited house, the personal representative files an affidavit with the clerk before closing out the estate. A quit claim deed passes whatever interest the grantor holds without any warranty of title.

sections.h2: How much does the Perry County Clerk charge to record documents?
sections.html:
The clerk publishes a minimum fee for each document type. These are the ones that come up most often in a sale or an estate:

Minimum recording fees posted by the Perry County Clerk
DocumentMinimum fee
Deed$50
Deed of correction$46
Easement$50
Mortgage$80
Release of mortgage, full or partial$46
Power of attorney$50
Affidavit of descent$50
Will$47
Certificate of delinquency release$46

Most items add $3 for each page past the fifth. A mortgage adds the same $3 only after page 30. The clerk's table is labeled as minimums, so a document with extra references or pages costs more.

sections.h2: How is the transfer tax figured on a Perry County sale?
sections.html:
The seller is the taxpayer. Kentucky's deed transfer tax under KRS 142.050 is a half dollar for each $500 of value, rounding any leftover amount up to the next $500. Perry County's Census median owner-occupied value is $91,800, which is 184 units of $500 and a tax of $92.00. The clerk gathers the tax before recording and keeps 5% of it for the service, sending the rest to the county treasurer every three months for the county's general fund.

The statute excuses a long list of transfers, including:

  • Deeds between spouses, or between former spouses as part of a divorce.
  • Foreclosure transfers and voluntary surrenders in lieu of foreclosure.
  • Sales for delinquent taxes and partition deeds.
  • Transfers between parent and child, or grandparent and grandchild, for nominal consideration.
  • Deeds that only secure or release a debt, and deeds that confirm or correct an earlier recorded deed.

For a gift or a nominal-price deed the tax is figured on the estimated open-market price. A clerk who records a taxable deed without collecting can be fined $50 under the same statute.

sections.h2: What happens to unpaid taxes and liens at the Perry County Clerk?
sections.html:
The clerk becomes the keeper of any property tax bill the sheriff could not collect. Under the Department of Revenue's process, bills transfer on April 15 and become certificates of delinquency recorded as liens. Interest runs at one percent a month, and the clerk and the county attorney each add a commission. The county attorney mails owners a 30-day notice and, if needed, a second notice, and the clerk holds the tax sale 90 to 135 days after transfer.

Perry County's clerk page directs buyers and owners to a delinquent tax application and says eligible owners can set up a payment plan with the county attorney. When a certificate is sold to an outside purchaser, the clerk's fee table shows a $30 charge to record the assignment and $46 to record a release. A seller with an open certificate should settle it with the clerk, get the release recorded, and bring proof to the closing so the title company can clear the lien.

sections.h2: Can Perry County Clerk staff search title or records for me?
sections.html:
No. The clerk's FAQ says deputy clerks cannot run a title search and may only help with a search the visitor performs. Requests for copies must be written and must include a book and page, an instrument number, or enough detail to find the document, such as the borrower, lender and loan amount. The office keeps a list of attorneys, paralegals and abstractors who do insured title work.

The clerk's site also promotes DocAlert, a free service from the records software vendor that emails an owner whenever a deed or mortgage is recorded in that person's name. For anyone selling a house that has sat vacant or passed through an estate, the alert is a cheap safeguard against a fraudulent filing.

sections.h2: What does the Perry County housing picture look like for sellers?
sections.html:
Perry County had 28,473 residents at the 2020 census, and the Census Bureau's 2025 estimate is 26,555, a 6.7% decline. In 2020 there were 11,481 households, 29.5% of them one person living alone, and the median age was 42.0. QuickFacts shows 2.42 people per household and 70.4% owner-occupancy for 2020 to 2024, with a median gross rent of $798 and median owner costs of $1,167 with a mortgage. Median household income is $42,181.

Hazard is the county seat and largest city. The county contains 343 square miles along the North and Middle Forks of the Kentucky River and is bordered by Breathitt, Knott, Letcher, Harlan, Leslie, Clay and Owsley counties. Two school systems serve it, Perry County Schools and Hazard Independent Schools, and Hazard Community and Technical College and the Hazard ARH Regional Medical Center are the best-known institutions.

faqs.q: What is the Perry County Clerk's address for deeds?
faqs.a: 481 Main Street, Suite 102, Hazard, KY 41701. The clerk's contact block shows weekday hours of 8:00 AM to 4:00 PM.

faqs.q: What is the clerk's fee for a Perry County deed?
faqs.a: Fifty dollars is the posted minimum, with $3 added per page beyond five. Transfer tax on the deed's stated value is separate.

faqs.q: Can closing documents be recorded electronically in Perry County?
faqs.a: Yes. The clerk's land records page lists Indecomm, CSC, Simplifile and ePN as e-recording services.

faqs.q: Who pays the transfer tax on a Perry County sale?
faqs.a: The seller pays it as grantor, at 50 cents for each $500 of value. A $91,800 deed produces $92.00.

faqs.q: Can the Perry County Clerk look up the owner of a parcel for me?
faqs.a: Staff will point you to the records but cannot perform a title search. Requests for copies must be in writing with a book and page, instrument number or similar detail.
